title: Introduction to manifoldsculpting
text: sim_s_curve() simulates S-curve paper, sheet bent shape sine wave, intrinsic coordinates u (arc length) v.  Manifold Sculpting preserves distances, embedding matches intrinsic coordinates rotation translation, without rescaling. best rotation:
code: set.seed(1) curve <- sim_s_curve(1000) x <- curve[c("x", "y", "z")]  set.seed(2) fit <- manifold_sculpting(x, ndim = 2, neighbors = 14) fit #> Manifold Sculpting embedding #> * 1000 samples, 3 variables to 2 dimensions #> * 14 neighbors, squishing rate 0.99 #> * 803 iterations (converged), final error 0.001557 library(ggplot2)  panels <- rbind(   data.frame(panel = "S-curve (x, y)", d1 = curve$x, d2 = curve$y, u = curve$u),   data.frame(panel = "Manifold Sculpting", d1 = fit$embedding[, 1],              d2 = fit$embedding[, 2], u = curve$u) ) panels$panel <- factor(panels$panel, levels = unique(panels$panel)) ggplot(panels, aes(d1, d2, color = u)) +   geom_point(size = 0.7) +   facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free") +   scale_color_viridis_c() +   labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +   theme_bw() truth <- scale(as.matrix(curve[c("u", "v")]), scale = FALSE) s <- svd(crossprod(fit$embedding, truth)) aligned <- fit$embedding %*% s$u %*% t(s$v) sqrt(mean(rowSums((aligned - truth)^2))) #> [1] 0.001510244

code: library(manifoldsculpting)  set.seed(42) roll <- sim_swiss_roll(2000) roll #> # A tibble: 2,000 × 5 #>        x      y      z     u      v #>    <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> #>  1  1.82  4.98  -0.832  2.96  4.98  #>  2  1.82  5.24  -0.841  2.97  5.24  #>  3  1.82 -2.57  -0.850  2.98 -2.57  #>  4  1.82  3.97  -0.859  2.98  3.97  #>  5  1.82  1.70  -0.868  2.99  1.70  #>  6  1.82  0.229 -0.877  3.00  0.229 #>  7  1.82  2.84  -0.886  3.01  2.84  #>  8  1.82 -4.38  -0.895  3.02 -4.38  #>  9  1.82  1.88  -0.904  3.03  1.88  #> 10  1.82  2.46  -0.913  3.04  2.46  #> # ℹ 1,990 more rows set.seed(1) fit <- manifold_sculpting(roll[c("x", "y", "z")], ndim = 2, neighbors = 20, nstart = 3) fit #> Manifold Sculpting embedding #> * 2000 samples, 3 variables to 2 dimensions #> * 20 neighbors, squishing rate 0.99 #> * 746 iterations (converged), final error 0.01363 #> * Best of 3 runs, with final errors 0.01363, 0.0142, 192.8 # Best rotation of the embedding onto (u, v) truth <- scale(as.matrix(roll[c("u", "v")]), scale = FALSE) s <- svd(crossprod(fit$embedding, truth)) aligned <- fit$embedding %*% s$u %*% t(s$v) sqrt(mean(rowSums((aligned - truth)^2))) # RMSE, the roll is 49 x 12 #> [1] 0.01832235

text: algorithm five steps: Find k nearest neighbors point. point \(p_i\) neighbor \(n_{ij}\), record distance \(\delta_{ij}\) , angle \(\theta_{ij}\) formed \(p_i\), \(n_{ij}\) \(m_{ij}\), neighbor \(n_{ij}\) colinear \(p_i\). average neighbor distance \(\delta_{ave}\). Rotate data onto principal components. first ndim components preserved dimensions; others scaled. Iterate: multiply scaled dimensions squishing_rate, scale preserved dimensions average neighbor distance \(\delta_{ave}\) . Visit points breadth-first, random point, move one preserved dimensions, hill climbing, minimize error $$\epsilon_i = \sum_j w_{ij} \left[    \left(\frac{\delta_{ij} - \delta_{ij}^0}{\delta_{ave}}\right)^2 +    \max\left(0, \frac{\theta_{ij}^0 - \theta_{ij}}{\pi}\right)^2    \right]$$ superscript 0 marks original values, weights \(w_{ij}\) higher neighbors already moved iteration. Drop scaled dimensions. weighting normalization error, adaptive step size hill climbing, stopping rule follow reference implementation authors Waffles library. Unlike Waffles, dimensions data kept (paper asks): scaled dimensions contribute distances angles common factor, contributions computed iterations work ndim preserved dimensions. Points breadth-first traversal reach also adjusted iteration. Like local optimization, iterations can end local minimum, part manifold folded another. final error tells runs apart: much larger run unfolded manifold. risk depends data, decreases neighbors runs (nstart). 2000 points Swiss roll sim_swiss_roll(), example, one run seven stays folded 20 neighbors (fewer points), best three runs reliable, S-curve sim_s_curve() unfolded 14 neighbors. neighbor search iterations written C++. algorithm uses random number generator R; call set.seed() first reproducible results.

title: Simulated manifolds — sim_manifolds
text: Swiss roll, \(t_i = 8i/n + 2\) \(0 \le < n\), $$x_i = t_i \sin(t_i), \quad y_i \sim U(-6, 6), \quad z_i = t_i \cos(t_i).$$ intrinsic coordinates arc length along roll, \(u_i = (\sinh^{-1}(t_i) + t_i \sqrt{t_i^2 + 1}) / 2\), \(v_i = y_i\). S-curve, \(t_i = (2.2i - 0.1)\pi / n\), $$x_i = t_i, \quad y_i = \sin(t_i), \quad z_i \sim U(0, 2).$$ intrinsic coordinates arc length along curve, \(u_i = \int_0^{t_i} \sqrt{\cos^2(w) + 1} \, dw\), \(v_i = z_i\). (paper gives \(v_i = y_i\), misprint since \(y_i\) function \(u_i\).)
